---
title: "coords"
subtitle: "Coordinates, projections, and grid-to-grid remapping"
---

## Overview

`coords` is the geometry and remapping core of `fesm-utils`. It is a clean
rebuild of the older `coordinates` library, keeping the user-facing API
(`points_class` / `grid_class` / `map_class`, `*_init`, `map_field`) while
replacing the internal storage, neighbour search and conservative remapping with
a single design. Everything is reached through one umbrella module:

```fortran
use coords
```

The package covers:

- **Coordinate and grid definition** — point sets (`points_class`) and regular
  grids (`grid_class`), each carrying a shared coordinate-system descriptor
  (`coord_system`: map type, units, planet, projection).
- **Map projections** — the oblimap2 oblique stereographic forward/inverse
  transforms, driven by projection parameters `(lambda, phi, alpha, x_e, y_n)`
  (for `polar_stereographic`, `phi` is the standard parallel and the projection
  is centred at the pole, on a sphere as on an ellipsoid),
  and transverse Mercator (e.g. UTM; `mtype="transverse_mercator"`, Snyder 1987)
  with `lambda` the central meridian, `phi` the latitude of origin, `k0` the
  scale factor and `x_e`/`y_n` the false easting/northing [m].
- **Gaussian-latitude grids** — quadrature latitudes for spectral/atmospheric
  grids (non-uniform y-axis).
- **k-d tree nearest-neighbour search** — the fast neighbour engine underneath
  distance-based maps.
- **Weight-map remapping** — one sparse source→target store applied with
  nearest-neighbour, Shepard (inverse-distance), quadrant, bilinear or
  conservative (area-weighted) kernels.
- **SCRIP-superset weight-map file I/O** — maps are cached as valid SCRIP
  remapping files, interoperable with `cdo` and other tools.
- **CDO grid-description interop and cached map generation** — read/write `cdo`
  griddes files, generate weights online (in-package or via an external `cdo`
  call), and load-if-exists / save-on-generate caching.
- **The multigrid coupler** — a thin registry + lazy map-cache layer for
  remapping fields between many named grids.

## Key derived types

All types are defined in `coordinates.f90` (geometry) and `mapping.f90` (maps),
and re-exported by `use coords`.

| Type | Role |
|------|------|
| `coord_system` | Coordinate-reference metadata (`mtype`, `units`, `planet`, `proj`, `xy_conv`, `is_cartesian`, `is_projection`, `is_lon180`). Defined once and embedded as `%cs` in every geometry type. |
| `points_class` | An unstructured set of points: `npts`, 1D arrays `x, y, lon, lat, area`, and `%cs`. |
| `grid_axis_class` | Regular axis description: `nx, ny, x0, dx, y0, dy`, the axis vectors `x(:), y(:)` (supports explicit non-uniform axes, e.g. Gaussian latitudes) and the cell edges `x_bnds(0:nx), y_bnds(0:ny)`. The edges are filled at `grid_init` (default: adjacent midpoints, half-cell extrapolation at the ends, `axis_midpoint_bounds`; `explicit_bnds` records given bounds) and are the one source of cell edges for `grid_area` and the conservative generators. |
| `grid_class` | A regular grid: `name`, axis block `%G` (`grid_axis_class`), 2D arrays `x, y, lon, lat, area`, and `%cs`. |
| `map_class` | Public map wrapper: source/target names (`name1`, `name2`), target coordinate system `%cs`, target axes `%G`, fixed interpolation `method`, and the internal weight store `%wm`. |
| `weight_map_t` | The single sparse source→target store (link-centric, SCRIP-style). Usually accessed only through `map_class`; see below. |
| `coupler_class` | A registry of named grids plus a lazily-built cache of grid→grid maps (`coupler.f90`). |

### The weight store

`weight_map_t` (module `weight_map`) is one sparse matrix with two payload
flavours, selected by `%kind`:

- `MAP_DISTANCE` — links carry the neighbour distance, position (`xn`, `yn`) and
  quadrant; the per-link weight is built at *apply* time from the chosen kernel.
  One cached distance map therefore serves `nn` / `quadrant` / `shepard` /
  `bilinear` and adapts to a time-varying source mask.
- `MAP_WEIGHT` — links carry a final baked weight `w(:)`; apply just reduces it
  (conservative maps, imported SCRIP maps, or precomputed bilinear).

Links are grouped by destination; `dst_off(:)` is a CSR offset array. The
type is rarely handled directly — `map_init` / `map_field` wrap it — but the
low-level API (`weight_map_alloc`, `weight_map_index`, `weight_map_apply`,
`weight_map_prune`, `weight_map_free`) is public for building custom maps.

## Core workflow

The typical use is: define a source and target grid, generate (or load) a weight
map between them, then apply that map to remap one or more fields.

```fortran
use coords

type(grid_class) :: gsrc, gtgt
type(map_class)  :: map
real(dp), allocatable :: field_src(:,:), field_tgt(:,:)

! 1. Define source and target grids (here two Cartesian grids in km).
call grid_init(gsrc, name="src", mtype="cartesian", units="kilometers", &
               x0=0.0_dp,   dx=100.0_dp, nx=10, y0=0.0_dp,   dy=100.0_dp, ny=10)
call grid_init(gtgt, name="tgt", mtype="cartesian", units="kilometers", &
               x0=150.0_dp, dx=100.0_dp, nx=7,  y0=150.0_dp, dy=100.0_dp, ny=7)

! 2. Generate (or load) a weight map. `method` fixes the kernel; the map is
!    cached under `fldr` and reloaded next time when load=.true. (the default).
call map_init(map, gsrc, gtgt, method="shepard", max_neighbors=8, fldr="maps")

! 3. Apply it. var1 is the source field; var2 is sized to the target grid.
allocate(field_src(10,10), field_tgt(7,7))
! ... fill field_src ...
call map_field(map, "myfield", field_src, field_tgt, stat="mean")
```

`grid_init` is generic and also accepts explicit axis vectors (`x=`, `y=`), an
existing grid/points object, or a file (`grid_init(grid, filename, ...)` reads a
`.nc` grid or a `/map/` namelist). Explicit cell bounds can be given with
`x_bnds=` / `y_bnds=` (`0:n`, validated: strictly monotonic, each centre inside
its cell; the other axis takes the default midpoint bounds). For a lat-lon or
Gaussian grid with explicit bounds, `grid%area` is the latitude-band area
(`R²·Δλ·(sin φ₂ - sin φ₁)` on a sphere, the authalic zone formula on an
ellipsoid); grids with default bounds keep the 4-corner area.

`grid_init_gaussian(grid, name, nlon, nlat [, planet, lon180, x0])` builds a
global Gaussian grid (`mtype="gaussian"`) whose latitude bounds come from the
Gauss weights, `sin φ_{j+1/2} = sin φ_{j-1/2} + w_j` from -1 to +1: the bands
reach the poles, each node lies inside its band, and the cell area is the
quadrature weight `R²·Δλ·w_j`. `planet` defaults to `"Spherical Earth"` here
(spectral models, SHTns, are spherical); other grids default to WGS84. A lat-lon → Gauss `con` map then integrates exactly
in the quadrature: `Σ_k Δλ·w_j·v_k` equals the band-metric source integral, with
no rescaling. `grid_cdo_write_desc_short` writes the bounds of such a grid as
cdo `xbounds`/`ybounds`, and `grid_cdo_read_desc` reads them back (only from
files with the fesm-utils header; existing descriptions read as before). Point sets are built the same way with
`points_init(pts, name=, mtype=, units=, x=, y=, ...)`.

`map_init` is overloaded for grid→grid, grid→points, points→grid,
points→points, and grid→grid *by name* (`map_init(map, name1, name2, ...)`,
which reads both grid descriptions from `grid_<name>.txt`). Key optional
arguments to the grid→grid form:

- `method` — interpolation kernel: `"con"` (conservative) or a distance kernel
  `"nn"` / `"shepard"` / `"quadrant"` / `"bilin"` (default `"nn"`).
- `gen` — generator used when weights must actually be built: `"coords"`
  (in-package, default) or `"cdo"` (external `cdo` system call).
- `fldr` — map cache directory (default `"maps"`).
- `load` — if `.true.` (default) an existing cache file is loaded instead of
  regenerated; freshly generated maps are always saved.
- `max_neighbors`, `dist_max` — neighbour-search controls for distance maps.
- `precompute_weights` — collapse a distance store to baked weights at init for
  `shepard`/`bilinear` (default `.true.`); the on-disk cache stays
  distance-format either way.
- `weight_cutoff` — relative cutoff for pruning sliver links from baked
  (`con`/bilinear) maps before caching: per target, links below
  `weight_cutoff·max(w)` are dropped (default `1e-4`; `0.0` keeps all links).
  The largest link of a target always survives; the coverage removed is kept
  (see *Normalisation and coverage*).
- `on_mismatch`, `hash_names` — cache identity, see *CDO interop and map caching*.

`map_field` is generic over the field element type (`integer`, `sp`, `dp`) and
over grid/points sources and targets. Beyond `stat` it accepts `method` (kernel
override for distance maps), `missing_value`, `radius`, `mask2`, `reset`,
`mask_pack`, and optional fill/filter post-processing (`fill_method`,
`filt_method`, `filt_par`). The `stat` argument selects the reduction over each
target's links: `"mean"` (default), `"count"` (weighted mode), or `"stdev"`.
The 8 real specifics also take `norm`, `frac2`, `area1` and `area2` (below).

### Normalisation and coverage

A conservative map made by the coords generator carries, besides its link
weights `w_jk` (overlap area in the map metric of the generator), the full cell
areas of source and target (`wfull_src`, `wfull_dst`) and the link sums before
pruning (`wcov_src`, `wcov_dst`), all in that metric; they are written to the
cache as `mp_wfull_*`, `mp_wcov_*`. With them, for target `k` and its valid
links `V_k` (`w > 0`, source value not missing), and
`φ_jk = q_j·w_jk/wfull_src_j` the fraction of source cell `j` lying in `k`
(`q`, `r` restore what pruning removed):

| Argument | Value at target `k` |
|---|---|
| `frac2` (`real(dp)`, target shape) | covered fraction `min(1, r_k·Σ_V w / wfull_dst_k)`; 0 where nothing valid is linked, outside `mask_pack`, or not mapped |
| `norm="frac"` (default) | `Σ_V w v / Σ_V w`: the covered mean (unchanged path) |
| `norm="dst"` | `r_k·Σ_V w v / wfull_dst_k` = `frac2·mean` (map metric) |
| `norm="dst"`, `area1` + `area2` | `Σ_V φ_jk·area1_j·v_j / area2_k`, exact in the model metric |
| `norm="sum"` | `Σ_V φ_jk·α_j·v_j`, `α = area1` if present, else 1 (amount per target) |

`area1` (source shape) and `area2` (target shape) are the model cell areas
(`real(dp)`). With `norm="dst"` and both areas, `Σ_k area2_k·v2_k =
Σ_j area1_j·v_j·Σ_k φ_jk` for any choice of areas: for a target that covers
the source, the integral is preserved. Rules: `norm /= "frac"` needs
`stat="mean"` and a conservative map (else an error); `frac2` on a
non-conservative map is `merge(1,0,mask2)`; `area1` without `area2` (or the
reverse) with `norm="dst"` is an error; fill/filter post-processing does not
change `frac2`. A `con` map without coverage data (a `cdo` map, or a cache file
written before coverage was stored) stops with "regenerate <file>" when `norm`
or `frac2` is requested. The 4 `int` specifics take none of these.

Geometry of `conservative_spherical` (projected source → lat-lon/Gauss
target). Each cell edge is subsampled into NSUB = 8 segments in the grid's own
plane (projection x-y, or rotated lon-lat) and every sample is inverse-projected
and joined by great-circle arcs, so a projected cell that straddles the 0/360
meridian or contains the pole is a proper spherical polygon. A target cell's
poleward parallel, traced by great-circle chords, is concave, so the source
polygon is clipped against the cell's 8 strips in longitude (each convex,
bounded by two meridians and one chord of each parallel) and the pieces are
summed; the strips of all target cells tile the sphere. Target longitudes come
from the unwrapped axis (as in the lat-lon → lat-lon path) and latitude bounds
are clamped to ±90. For a target that covers the source domain, `Σ_k φ_jk = 1`
to ~1e-12 on a spherical planet (up to ~2e-10 for a cell that holds the pole,
round-off over its ~1500 polar strip pieces) and to ~1e-8 on WGS84 (the pieces
have great-circle edges, and their geodesic areas on the ellipsoid do not add up
exactly). Each source polygon is built once (source-major loop over a k-d tree
of the target centres); polygons with repeated vertices (a cell with two
corners at a pole) are reduced to distinct vertices, candidate pairs whose
bounding spherical caps do not meet are not clipped, and a source polygon that
lies inside one strip takes its own area as the overlap. The links of each
target are stored in ascending source order for any thread count. ANT-16KM →
T64 (WGS84): 4.3 s serial, 0.8 s on 10 threads.

## Remapping kernels

The kernel is fixed when the map is generated (it is part of the cache key) and
selected via `method`:

- **`nn` (nearest)** — copies the single nearest valid source value. Use for
  categorical/index fields, masks, and where no smoothing is wanted.
- **`shepard`** — inverse-distance-squared weighting over the neighbours within
  `radius`. A good general-purpose smooth interpolation for scattered or
  point-set sources.
- **`quadrant`** — nearest valid neighbour in each of the four quadrants, IDW
  combined; more isotropic than plain Shepard near data gaps.
- **`bilin` (bilinear)** — for structured source→target pairs, exact index-space
  bilinear interpolation (matches `cdo genbil`). Best for smooth fields on
  regular grids; bakes to a `MAP_WEIGHT` map.
- **`con` (conservative)** — area-weighted overlap via analytic polygon
  clipping. Conserves the area integral, so it is the right choice for fluxes and
  for aggregating a fine grid onto a coarse one. Built as a `MAP_WEIGHT` map.

Distance kernels (`nn`/`shepard`/`quadrant`) share a single `MAP_DISTANCE`
store, so the kernel can also be overridden per call in `map_field(method=)`
without rebuilding the map. Conservative and bilinear are baked weights and are
fixed at generation.

## CDO interop and map caching

Grids round-trip through `cdo` griddes text files (module `grid_cdo`):

- `grid_cdo_write_desc_short(grid, fldr)` writes `grid_<name>.txt`, a
  `cdo`-compliant description with a `#`-comment header carrying the full
  `coord_system` so the grid can be reconstructed exactly.
- `grid_cdo_read_desc(grid, name, fldr)` rebuilds a `grid_class` from such a
  file (the reader falls back on the CF `grid_mapping_name` for files stripped of
  the `fesm-utils` header, e.g. native `cdo` descriptions).

Map caching is handled inside `map_init`. The cache filename is derived from the
two grid names, the folder and the method (`gen_map_filename`), and:

1. if `load=.true.` (default) and the file exists, the map is loaded, with the
   file format auto-detected — an in-package cache (carries a `meta` variable) vs
   a standard/`cdo` SCRIP file;
2. otherwise the weights are generated (in-package for `gen="coords"`, or by an
   external `cdo gen<method>` call for `gen="cdo"`) and saved to the cache.

Cache identity. Each new cache file (in-package or `cdo`) carries global
attributes `coords_src_sig`, `coords_dst_sig` (grid signatures:
`grid_signature_str(grid)`, the coordinate system, the axis sizes and the
first/last/sum of the axes and bounds), `coords_method`, `coords_gen`,
`coords_weight_cutoff` and `coords_format`. On load (`map_init` with a cached
file), the file is checked against the grids:

- signatures present and different (`grid_signature_match`, tolerance 1e-9 of a
  cell, so a grid read back from `grid_<name>.txt` still matches):
  `on_mismatch="error"` (default) stops and names both signatures and the file;
  `on_mismatch="rebuild"` regenerates and overwrites the file (logged);
- no signatures (a file written before signatures, or by another tool): loaded
  as before, with a one-time "unverified" log line;
- `n_src` / `n_dst` that do not match the grid sizes always stop.

By default the file name stays `scrip-<method>_<src>_<dst>.nc`. With
`map_init(..., hash_names=.true.)` (or `coupler_init(..., hash_names=.true.)`)
it is `scrip-<method>_<src>-<h8>_<dst>-<h8>.nc`, where `h8 = grid_hash8(grid)`
(FNV-1a over the signature at 6 significant digits), so two grids with one name
can coexist in one folder. A legacy file of the same size but other axes is
accepted unverified: clear the map folder (or rename the grid) when a grid
definition changes at equal size.

Because the cache is always a valid SCRIP remapping file, a `cdo`-generated map
and an in-package `coords` map interoperate at the same filename. The file I/O
primitives are public as `weight_map_write` / `weight_map_read` (module
`map_io`); `map_read(map, src_name, dst_name, fldr, method)` loads a pre-existing
SCRIP map directly into a `map_class`.

## Coupler

The `coupler` module (module `coupler`, `use coupler`) sits on top of the mapping
core and manages many grids at once. A `coupler_class` holds a registry of named
grids and a lazily populated cache of grid→grid maps: grids are nodes, maps are
directed, method-typed edges.

```fortran
use coords
use coupler

type(coupler_class)   :: cpl
type(grid_class)      :: gcoarse, gfine
real(dp), allocatable :: fs(:,:), ft(:,:)

call coupler_init(cpl, map_fldr="maps")          ! empty registry + cache
                                                 ! [, gen, on_mismatch, hash_names]
call coupler_add_grid(cpl, "coarse", gcoarse)    ! register grids by name
call coupler_add_grid(cpl, "fine",   gfine)

! remap sizes the destination itself; the (src,dst,method) map is built on first
! use and reused thereafter. method defaults to "con".
call remap(cpl, fs, "coarse", ft, "fine", method="bilin")
```

- `coupler_add_grid(cpl, name, grid)` registers a copy of a grid (once, at
  init); `coupler_take_grid(cpl, name, grid)` moves an allocatable grid in
  without a copy (for very large grids). Unregistered names are resolved on
  demand from `grid_<name>.txt` in the map folder, read once into a "from
  disk" slot and reused. Registering a name that is already a from-disk slot
  is a no-op if the grids agree and an error otherwise.
- `remap(cpl, var_src, src, var_dst, dst, method, stat, missing_value, mask2,
  reset, mask_pack, fill_method, filt_method, filt_par, norm, frac2)` finds-or-builds the map
  for `(src, dst, method)`, allocates `var_dst` to the target size, and applies
  it with `map_field`, to which the optional arguments are passed unchanged. It
  is overloaded for `dp` / `sp` / `int` and 2D / 3D fields (the `int`
  specifics take `missing_value, mask2, reset, mask_pack`; for 3D, `mask2` and
  `frac2` are 3D and the map is applied per layer). With `reset=.false.`, `var_dst` must
  already be allocated at the target shape. `method` is part of the cache key;
  `stat` and the rest are forwarded per call and are not.
- `method="auto"` resolves per call: `"con"` for `norm="dst"`/`"sum"`
  (amounts are remapped conservatively both ways); otherwise `"bilin"` when the target is finer than
  the source (smaller median model cell area, i.e. refining) and `"con"` when
  it is coarser or equal. The model cell area is the plane `dx·dy` for a
  projected grid and `grid%area·xy_conv²` otherwise.
- `remap` with `src == dst` copies the field (no map, no registration needed):
  `mask_pack`, `reset`, `fill_method` and `filt_*` still apply, `mask2` is
  `var /= missing_value`, and `stat="stdev"` gives 0.
- `coupler_method(cpl, src, dst [, method, norm])` returns the method `remap`
  would use for the same arguments (`"auto"` resolved) without building or
  applying a map, e.g. to log it.
- `coupler_prime(cpl, src, dst, method, gen)` eagerly builds a map up front
  (fail-fast at init rather than mid-timestep) and is the point at which a map's
  generator can be overridden via `gen=`. It is a no-op for `src == dst`.

### Global ↔ regional exchange

Each registered grid carries a *model cell area* `[m²]`, the area its model
integrates over: by default the plane `dx·dy` for a projected grid (what Yelmo
and FastIsostasy integrate) and `grid%area·xy_conv²` otherwise.
`coupler_set_area(cpl, name, area)` overrides it (e.g. the Gaussian quadrature
`R²·Δλ·w_j` of a spectral model). `remap` with `norm="dst"` / `"sum"` passes the
registered areas of both grids as `area1` / `area2`, so mass accounting and the
integral below share one metric per grid (an identity remap with `norm="sum"`
returns `v·area`).

- `coupler_integral(cpl, name, var [, mask, missing_value, describe])` returns
  `Σ area·var` (Neumaier-compensated) with the registered areas; with
  `describe=.true.` it logs this integral next to the one over the ellipsoidal
  cell areas (`grid%area`), as a diagnostic of the metric difference (several %
  for a polar stereographic ice grid). For a regional → global `remap` with
  `norm="dst"`, the global integral equals the covered part of the regional one
  to rounding.
- Merge of N regional fields and a background onto a global grid, in
  accumulator form:

  ```fortran
  type(coupler_merge_t) :: acc
  call coupler_merge_begin(acc, cpl, "T64" [, kind="extensive"|"intensive"])
  call coupler_merge_add(acc, cpl, "ANT", h_ant [, owner=o_ant, missing_value=])
  call coupler_merge_add(acc, cpl, "GRL", h_grl [, owner=o_grl])
  call coupler_merge_end(acc, cpl, background, h_glob [, frac_tot=, overlap_tol=])
  ```

  Per domain `d` (valid cells `j`, owner weight `o_dj`, default 1) and target
  cell `k`: coverage `F_dk = r_k Σ_j w_jk o_dj / wfull_k`; amount
  `A_dk = Σ_j φ_jk o_dj area_j v_j / area_k` (extensive) or
  `r_k Σ_j w_jk o_dj v_j / wfull_k` (intensive). With `F = Σ_d F_d`:
  extensive `var = (1 - min(F,1))·bg + Σ_d A_d` (regional amounts are never
  rescaled; only the background is capped), intensive
  `var = (1 - min(F,1))·bg + Σ_d A_d / max(F,1)` (preserves a constant).
  Domains are summed in the order of their names, so the result does not depend
  on the order of `coupler_merge_add` calls; adding a domain twice is an error.
  `max(F) > 1 + overlap_tol` (default `1e-2`) stops and names the overlapping
  domains; a smaller excess is accepted and the double-counted amount logged.
- `coupler_owner_reduce(cpl, src_hi, owner_hi, dst, owner)` removes from
  `owner` (on `dst`) the part already owned by the higher-priority domain:
  `owner := max(0, owner - covered fraction of owner_hi)`. Call it once at init,
  in priority order, to make `Σ_d o_d = 1` where domains overlap.
- `coupler_split(cpl, src, var_src, dst, var_dst [, method, ref_src, ref_dst,
  missing_value, fill_method, mask2])`: global → regional. Without references
  it is `remap` (default `method="bilin"`); with both,
  `var_dst = ref_dst + remap(var_src - ref_src)`, where a missing anomaly counts
  as 0 (the reference is kept). One reference without the other is an error.

Each map is built once, stored once, and shared across all callers. Grids and
maps live in allocatable slot arrays without a fixed capacity: when an array
grows, each slot's grid / map is moved (`move_alloc`), never copied, and maps
are built directly from the registered grids.

## Bit-identity gate

`test/coords/test_coupler_bitident.f90` runs a fixed call set of the coupler
and `map_field` (con/bilin/nn; dp/sp/int; stat variants; `reset=.false.`,
`mask_pack`, fill/filter; 3D; grid ↔ points; every conservative generator path)
and writes each result, the grid geometry and the map weights to
`bitident_out/<case>.bin`. `make check` runs it for its in-binary checks
(`remap` = direct `map_field`). To compare against a reference commit:

```bash
test/coords/bitident.sh <ref-commit>               # gen + cached
BITIDENT_MODES=cached test/coords/bitident.sh <ref> # across a change of new maps
```

The script builds the working-tree copy of the test at `<ref-commit>` (in a
temporary git worktree, with the compiler block of the current root
`Makefile`) and at the working tree, and compares every stream with `cmp`:
`gen` (maps generated by each build) and `cached` (both load the cache files
the reference generated).
